title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The cote mixes Grothendieck's 1965 notes on a 'Galois theory of motives' with drafts of other texts; the neighbouring pages are an unrelated analysis draft on Frobenius and Cauchy majorants. This page concerns a central simple algebra C over the fraction field K of a Dedekind ring A, a maximal order σ in C, its units σ*, its automorphism group Aut(σ), and its outer automorphisms Autext(σ). The underlying exact sequence is 1 → G_m → σ* → Aut(σ) → Autext(σ) → … → Pic(A), with Autext(σ) related to Picent(σ) and two-sided ideals. Grothendieck's notations appear to be: Is(C) for the isomorphism classes of maximal orders (or of their models), Brd(C) for a local 'Brauer/ramification' invariant, and Ram(C/A) for the ramification locus.

(1) Local case ('cas Brauer'). Take A complete or local Dedekind with Pic(A)=0, and C a division algebra of index e. Then the maximal order σ is unique, so Is(C)=1. By Skolem–Noether every automorphism of σ is conjugation by an element of the normaliser N(σ). We have N(σ)/K*σ* ≅ Z/eZ, generated by a uniformiser Π of C. Hence Autext(σ) = Brd(C) = Z/eZ. This is a local obstruction to automorphisms being inner: there are e classes of automorphisms of σ modulo inner ones.

(2) Global case. Suppose automorphisms of σ are locally inner outside Ram(C/A). An automorphism then gives a section of σ*/G_{m,A}, i.e. of the sheaf of 'projective units'. The obstruction to lifting this section to σ* is a class in H^1(A, G_m) = Pic(A), coming from H^1(A, σ*). Equivalently it gives a trivial class in Is(C). He notes this was already visible from earlier exact sequences.

(3) Deuring case. C is the quaternion algebra over Q ramified exactly at p and ∞, and σ = End(E) for a supersingular curve E over F_p-bar. He writes a six-term exact sequence:

Z/2 → σ* → Aut(σ) → Z/2 → π0(C,x) → π0(O,·) → 1.

This is the homotopy exact sequence of the functor E ↦ End(E) from the groupoid of supersingular elliptic curves to the groupoid of maximal orders of C. Its terms are:
- π1(C,x) = Aut(E) = σ*. This is Z/2 except Z/4 for j=1728 and Z/6 for j=0 when p ≠ 2,3.
- The first Z/2 = {±1} is the kernel of Aut(E) → Aut(End E), acting by conjugation.
- Aut(σ) → Z/2 records the local outer automorphism at p (e=2), i.e. conjugation by Π with Π² ~ p. This Z/2 is 'generated by Frobenius', since End(E^(p)) ≅ End(E) via the Frobenius isogeny.
- Aut(σ) → Z/2 is onto exactly when E descends to F_p, i.e. j ∈ F_p.
- π0(C) = supersingular isomorphism classes (Hasse invariant zero) modulo E ↦ E^(p).
- π0(O) = conjugacy classes (types) of maximal orders.

The upshot is that the type number equals the number of supersingular j-invariants modulo Gal(F_{p^2}/F_p). A marginal note asks for which p the values j=0 and j=1728 are supersingular. The last line, 'Question : σ* est-il pas égal…', is cut off.
errors: The first Z/2 must be the centre {±1} of σ*, i.e. the kernel of conjugation, not the kernel of the map to σ*. With that reading the sequence is a correct homotopy exact sequence of groupoids.

The statement 'σ* = Z/2 except j=0, 1728' tacitly requires those j to be supersingular for the given p (p≡2 mod 3 for j=0, p≡3 mod 4 for j=1728). His marginal note asks exactly this, so it is a gap rather than an error.

The 'local' identification Brd(C) = Autext(σ) = Z/eZ holds for the maximal order of a division algebra over a complete DVR. It is stated loosely with 'A Dedekind local' and without specifying the residue field, which is fine for local fields.

ideas.what: Outer automorphisms of a local maximal order equal Z/e (normaliser modulo K*σ*, generated by a uniformiser)
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of maximal order / local Picent of a maximal order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse, Eichler); see Reiner 'Maximal Orders'; Fröhlich 1973 for Picent

ideas.what: Global exact sequence: units → automorphisms → outer automorphisms → Pic(A) obstruction via H^1(A, σ*) and σ*/G_m
ideas.modern_name: Fröhlich–Reiner exact sequences for Picent / automorphisms of orders
ideas.where_published: Related nonabelian H^1 / gerbe yoga appears in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne (1971), not this specific case

ideas.what: Deuring correspondence written as the homotopy exact sequence of the groupoid map {supersingular curves} → {maximal orders}, with the Frobenius twist E ↦ E^(p) identified with the local outer automorphism at p
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence; type number = number of supersingular j modulo Frobenius
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941); refinements Ibukiyama, Kaneko; categorical form Kohel, Voight's 'Quaternion Algebras' ch. 42

ideas.what: For which p are j=0 and j=1728 supersingular
ideas.modern_name: Supersingularity of CM curves (p≡2 mod 3, p≡3 mod 4)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the Deuring correspondence as a fibration of groupoids (curves → maximal orders) with fibre Z/2, the fibre being the local outer automorphism at the ramified prime. The six-term exact sequence encodes both the automorphism groups and the 2-to-1 map onto types. This is a clean 'stacky' packaging that predates the standard categorical treatments, but the content is classical.
missed.quote: Z/2Z → σ* → Aut(σ) → Z/2Z → π0(C,x) → π0(O,∘) → 1 ... engendré par Frobenius
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's interest in the Deuring correspondence as a test case for 'motivic' Galois/gerbe descriptions (End of motives as orders), in the context of the motifs notes. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: All the mathematics (local outer automorphisms Z/e, Picent obstruction sequences, Deuring correspondence with Frobenius pairing) is classical. The only notable feature is the groupoid-homotopy packaging and its presence in the 1965 motives notes.
transcription_corrections: 'Brd(C) = Z/eZ' is annotated '(ramification)' underneath; 'Pic(A) = 0' sits below Is(C)=1.
'de[?] tels que' is probably 'de [C] tels que' or 'des tels que'.
'pour C type J[?]' is likely 'pour C type quaternionique/Jacobson' — unclear; 'par exemple' is readable.
The Deuring header likely reads 'Cas des corps gauches de Deuring, ramifiés en p et ∞' (not 'splittés').
Under σ*: 'sauf si j=0 ou j=12³ (i.e. on trouve Z/4Z resp. Z/6Z si p≠2,3)'; note that j=12³=1728 corresponds to Z/4 and j=0 to Z/6.
Under π0(C,x): 'classes d'iso. des classes de courbes elliptiques de Hasse nul modulo l'opération de Frobenius déduite de E ↦ E^(p)'; 'Hom nul' should be 'Hasse nul'.
The margin note: 'on voudrait savoir pour quels p ces j sont d'invariant de Hasse nul'.
The last line is probably 'Question : σ* est-il pas égal …' (cut off).
